classification.difficultyReason: Plot each coordinate point, apply the same supplied horizontal and vertical shift, and read and label its image coordinates.

content.prompt:
Mark the following points on your graph paper and translate each one 2 units right and 3 units up. Be careful to label each point and its image. Also write down the coordinates of each image point.

Use labelled $x$- and $y$-axes. One number plane may be used for all four parts if the points are neatly labelled.

answer.worked:
Move $A$ 2 grid units right and 3 grid units up and label the image $A'$.

$$A'=(0+2,0+3)=(2,3).$$

Move $B$ 2 grid units right and 3 grid units up and label the image $B'$.

$$B'=(2+2,1+3)=(4,4).$$

Move $C$ 2 grid units right and 3 grid units up and label the image $C'$.

$$C'=(-3+2,1+3)=(-1,4).$$

Move $D$ 2 grid units right and 3 grid units up and label the image $D'$.

$$D'=(-5+2,-5+3)=(-3,-2).$$

spec.description: One shared Cartesian plane with unit grid, numbered axes, original points and labelled image points. Prime labels distinguish images without requiring colour.
